problem: Let $F=GF(11)$ be a finite field of 11 elements. Let $G$ be the group of all non-singular $n \times n$ matrices over $F$. Let $H$ be the subgroup of those matrices whose determinant is 1. Determine the index $[G:H]$. \( \text{Express your answer as a single number.} \)
paragraphs: We need answer math. We need reason step by step. Problem: F=GF(11), G=GL(n,F) all nonsingular n x n matrices. H=SL(n,F) determinant 1. Determine index [G:H]. Express as single number.

Need think: For finite field GF(q), determinant map det: GL(n,q) -> F^* (multiplicative group), surjective, kernel SL(n,q). Index = |F^*| = q-1 = 10. Is there any nuance? For n? For n>=1. For n=1, GL(1,11)=F^*, SL(1,11)={1}, index 10. For n>=2 same. So answer 10.

Need provide reasoning maybe determinant homomorphism. Since every nonzero scalar can be determinant via diagonal matrix diag(a,1,...,1), surjective. Kernel determinant 1. So quotient GL/SL ≅ F^*, size 10.
Need ensure no hidden: G is group of all non-singular n x n matrices over F, H subgroup determinant 1. Index [G:H] = 10. final boxed.
answer_text:
The determinant gives a homomorphism

\[
\det: G = GL(n,F) \to F^* = GF(11)^\times.
\]

Its kernel is precisely

\[
H = \{A \in GL(n,F) : \det(A)=1\} = SL(n,F).
\]

The determinant map is surjective, since for any nonzero \(a \in F\), the matrix

\[
\operatorname{diag}(a,1,\dots,1)
\]

has determinant \(a\). Therefore,

\[
[G:H] = |G/H| = |F^*| = 11-1 = 10.
\]

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
